issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a public class named 'AnimalFarm' and contains duplicated/malformed content (including a repeated 'package' declaration and a second 'AnimalFarm' block), whereas the problem statement UML and the reference solution define a class named 'Farm'. Because the filename is Farm.java, this name mismatch and the malformed content will cause compilation errors and will block students from implementing the expected 'Farm' class as described in the assignment.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the contents of src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java in the template with a proper skeleton matching the UML and the solution: declare 'public class Farm' (name must match the filename), remove any duplicated 'package' declarations and extraneous duplicated class blocks, and provide the expected fields and method signatures so students can implement them. At minimum add: a private List<Animal> animals; a no-arg constructor that initializes animals = new ArrayList<>(); public List<Animal> getAnimals(); public void setAnimals(List<Animal>); public void addAnimal(Animal); public void feedAllAnimals(); public void singFarmSong(); and a private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal).
